Houston NDT schools by name: San Jacinto, Lone Star, UTI, private schools, the union route and online + practical

The route table above compares an NDT school, ASNT Houston and the Atlantis model in general terms. This section names the schools. Of the metros we reviewed for these pages, Houston has the widest choice of NDT training providers, from community college degrees to private schools to a union route, and they produce different kinds of training records.

Which schools teach NDT in Houston?

  • San Jacinto College. A stacked Nondestructive Testing Technology pathway: a Certificate of Technology of about six months, a Level 2 Certificate of about a year and a half, and an associate of applied science of about two years and 60 credits. It covers VT, MT, PT, UT, ET and radiography, and the college says it prepares students for ASNT, API, AWS and NACE certification paths.
  • Lone Star College. An Inspection Technology programme with short credentials, such as the one-semester, 15-credit Ultrasonic Examination Certificate Level I, whose courses the college says exceed SNT-TC-1A. In October 2025 its East Aldine Center announced a three-year partnership with Evident that equips students with five Epoch 650 flaw detectors.
  • UTI Houston (MIAT College of Technology). A nine-month Advanced Non-Destructive Testing Technician programme covering eddy current, visual, magnetic particle, ultrasonic, radiographic and penetrant testing, radiation safety and a capstone.
  • Private NDT schools. NDT Consultancy Services (NDTCS) in northwest Houston runs in-person and online Level I and II courses in MT, PT, VT, UT, ET and MFL, plus thickness and phased array, and says certification follows SNT-TC-1A and is the employer's responsibility. It lists itself as a Texas Workforce Commission eligible training provider.
  • The union route. The Operating Engineers' Local 112 offers a union path: it trains NDT people and sends them to oil and gas contractors around the country.
  • The local professional network. ASNT's section meeting listings include the Greater Houston Section, where working technicians and Level IIIs meet.

Why the school record matters to Houston employers

The large service companies say so in their postings. MISTRAS listings for Level II technicians at its Gulf Coast and Midwest offices accept three routes: graduation from an NDT technical programme that meets SNT-TC-1A, a prior Level II with a year of experience, or a Level I with enough field hours to certify to Level II. That first route only works if the school's record shows the hours by method and level. A diploma that lists a programme name but not the hours is harder for an employer's Level III to accept.

How to choose among Houston NDT schools

  • Ask for the hours breakdown. Method by method, Level I and Level II, set against SNT-TC-1A's recommended minimums.
  • Match methods to the Ship Channel. Refinery and petrochemical employers lean on UT thickness, MT, PT and VT; check the programme covers them at Level II.
  • Count the instrument time. How many hours do students spend on flaw detectors and real flawed specimens?
  • Ask who certifies. No Houston school certifies you under SNT-TC-1A. Your employer does, after its own exams.
  • Check rotation fit. A full-time programme rules out working turnarounds while you study; self-paced theory does not.
  • Funding. If you plan to use workforce or veteran funding, confirm the specific programme is approved for it before you enrol.

Where the Atlantis route fits among Houston providers

Atlantis is not a school and keeps no classroom in Houston. Study happens online at whatever pace your rotation allows, an ASNT NDT Level III fields course questions, and the course unlocks as soon as you enrol. Practice runs in the process plant and other workplaces of the Practical NDT simulator. Your employer provides the equipment, specimens and SNT-TC-1A-based written practice for the hands-on practical and exam, and certifies you. The Atlantis training record lists hours and topics by method and level, so the employer's Level III can measure it.

That suits a technician already on a Houston payroll who needs a method added without missing a turnaround. A school leaver with no employer may prefer a college programme for its lab time first. For Ship Channel work, the common starting methods are UT, MT, PT or VT, after NDT Level 1 training. Revise with the free practice tests. Houston inspection companies taking on trainees can use SNT-TC-1A training programme set-up.
